best_practice: The 'dynamic_agent_client' OAuth registration lets an agent install register itself and run on the user's existing ChatGPT plan with no API key or billing setup.
biggest_gap: The standard key path still needs phone OTP and prepaid credit before the first call, and there is no product MCP for account or key operations.

best_practice: A keyless CLI OAuth login (`ant auth login --no-browser`) that issues a workspace-scoped token, so an agent never handles a long-lived secret.
biggest_gap: Credits must be bought before the first call, and the Admin API deliberately can't mint usable keys.

best_practice: The product MCP sits at api.mistral.ai/mcp and uses the same API key, so once you have a key it is one command to connect.
biggest_gap: The MCP has no OAuth, so an agent still has to get a key a human copied out of the dashboard. The phone OTP gates the free tier.

best_practice: Free tier with no card and no phone. One email or Google click gets a usable key in about 2 minutes.
biggest_gap: There is no agent-native auth at all, and the only MCP is a local uvx package that needs a pasted key.

best_practice: A 'Coding agent setup' page that ships skills and a docs MCP together, with install commands for every major agent.
biggest_gap: No free tier: a $15 prepaid card purchase is required before the first API call.

best_practice: The hosted MCP uses OAuth and scoped consent, so 'no API keys are copied into the client'. They also retired the local key-based server in its favor.
biggest_gap: OAuth relies on CIMD only (no DCR), so clients without CIMD support need a key. Email verification is still a human step for email signups.

best_practice: One CLI handles login, every API call and the MCP server (`dg mcp`), so an agent installs one binary and inherits its auth.
biggest_gap: The advertised docs MCP endpoints return 401, and the product MCP is local-only (stdio/SSE) with no hosted OAuth server.

best_practice: Agent Skills document the SDK's non-obvious behaviour (silently ignored params, content=None), aimed at what models tend to get wrong.
biggest_gap: No way for an agent to get a credential without a human in the dashboard: no CLI login, no OAuth MCP, no key API. The dashboard returns a Cloudflare challenge to non-browser clients.

best_practice: Anonymous, claimable sandbox (`stripe sandbox create`) gated by proof-of-work instead of signup/captcha - the agent builds first, the human claims later.
biggest_gap: Anonymous sandbox expires in 7 days and the MCP/CLI need an admin toggle on existing accounts; the 2026-10-31 key-policy change will break existing MCP configs using plain secret keys.

best_practice: A dedicated machine-readable docs tree (/docs/build/llm-docs/*.md) with an explicit instructions-for-agents block inside llms.txt.
biggest_gap: No CLI/device login or scoped keys; key secret is shown once and regenerating needs a mobile OTP, so an agent can't rotate or mint keys on its own.

best_practice: Separate sandbox MCP host (mcp.sandbox.paypal.com) so agents can be pointed at test data by URL alone.
biggest_gap: Local MCP needs a raw OAuth access token that expires (~hours), forcing manual refresh; no CLI/device login.

best_practice: Every docs page has a .md twin with machine frontmatter (source_url, last_modified) plus an in-page 'For LLMs' instruction.
biggest_gap: No self-serve instant sandbox and no remote/OAuth MCP; MCP docs last modified 2025-06 (looks stale).

best_practice: CLI `login` that pulls API keys into local config so the agent never handles copy-pasted secrets, with explicit agent-mode (--json, stderr diagnostics, exit codes).
biggest_gap: The remote MCP only works for Production-approved teams, so the zero-to-MCP path for a new developer is local-only.

best_practice: Sharded llms.txt per product line (/docs/_llms/payments.txt etc.) keeps agent context small.
biggest_gap: No CLI or programmatic key minting; every key generation needs a human OTP.

best_practice: Versioned API reference as Markdown (2026q3 / preview / legacy) so agents can pin to the right API version.
biggest_gap: No self-serve sandbox credentials and no MCP.

best_practice: Granular OAuth scopes published in the MCP protected-resource metadata, so the user approves only what the agent needs.
biggest_gap: Remote MCP is production-only; agents testing safely must fall back to a local server with a full-access token.

best_practice: get-started.md: a playbook written for the agent to execute ('Perform actions yourself... Pause only for user authentication'), plus `vercel signup` so the agent can start account creation itself
biggest_gap: MCP OAuth is limited to Vercel-approved clients even though DCR exists, so custom agents and new clients are locked out. Claim Deployments needs the agent operator's own account

best_practice: `netlify login --request`: the agent gets a URL to hand the human and a URL to poll, so login works even when the agent is not on the user's machine
biggest_gap: Anonymous mode covers deploys only (claim window just 1 hour); no scoped or fine-grained tokens and no API to mint them

best_practice: `wrangler deploy --temporary`: a temporary account + scoped token + claim URL, advertised by the CLI itself when an agent is unauthenticated
biggest_gap: The classic dashboard signup is still behind a JS challenge, Turnstile and email verification, and the many separate product MCP servers fragment discovery (mitigated by the unified mcp.cloudflare.com)

best_practice: MCP URL params (project_ref, read_only=true, features=...) plus OAuth scopes give agents least-privilege access without custom tokens
biggest_gap: No anonymous or claimable database for a lone agent (claim tokens exist only for platforms with their own org), so a human account is always needed first

best_practice: auth.md: a spec-like, agent-addressed provisioning procedure (anonymous identity, jwt-bearer token, credentials, device-code claim) that is reachable straight from llms.txt
biggest_gap: Unclaimed projects die at 72h and DATABASE_URL rotates on claim, so the agent must re-fetch credentials. The domain move from neon.tech and the CLI rename from neonctl to neon may confuse agents trained on older data

best_practice: Docs Article/Search APIs that return markdown, documented in llms.txt as the preferred LLM access path
biggest_gap: Remote MCP OAuth only works for hosts with a pre-registered GitHub App (no DCR), so most CLI agents fall back to copying a PAT by hand

best_practice: agents.md tells the agent to keep working while waiting for the human ('Do not stop working while you wait'), references secrets only by env-var name, and explains the OAuth-expiry vs API-key trade-off
biggest_gap: Unscoped, non-expiring, account-wide API keys created only in the dashboard, plus no DCR, mean a human must copy a god-mode key for any non-blessed agent

best_practice: auth.md + RFC 9727 api-catalog + RFC 9728/8414 metadata: one 401 from the MCP teaches a client the whole auth chain, and the doc tells agents which credential type to use
biggest_gap: No anonymous or claimable project deploy (only a VM). Unverified trials get restricted networking. Tokens can only be minted in the dashboard

best_practice: MCP accepts the same personal API key as a bearer header (plus a dedicated /mcp/readonly endpoint), so headless agents never need a browser OAuth dance.
biggest_gap: No official CLI with device login and no llms-full.txt; API key creation still requires clicking through the web settings UI.

best_practice: Every .md doc page begins with a pointer telling agents to fetch llms.txt first, and PATs eliminated the old 'share every page with your integration' trap.
biggest_gap: Remote MCP is OAuth-only (no PAT bearer documented) and still labelled Beta in its resource metadata; local server abandoned.

best_practice: Scoped API tokens with mandatory expiry (1-365 days) plus a service-account API key path for headless MCP.
biggest_gap: No llms.txt/markdown docs and MCP API-token auth is off until an org admin flips it; v1->v2 URL churn leaves directory listings stale.

best_practice: Markdown docs carry agentTools frontmatter pointing agents back to the llms.txt project index.
biggest_gap: MCP v2 forces users to register their own OAuth client (client id/secret + exact redirect URIs) for Claude Code/Cursor/VS Code/Codex.

best_practice: Token-creation deep link with the exact MCP scopes pre-selected in the query string - the human only clicks Create.
biggest_gap: No llms-full.txt or official OpenAPI spec for the REST API; CLI has no browser/device login.

best_practice: An Agent CLI built for agents: self-describing --help, dry-run mode for every write, installable skills, and an install prompt to paste into the agent.
biggest_gap: Remote MCP has no DCR - outside the pre-built Claude/ChatGPT connectors, users must create an MCP connector app to get OAuth credentials.

best_practice: Per-product llms-*.txt files with an explicit instruction block telling LLM agents which official docs to prefer.
biggest_gap: Hosted MCP is off by default, requires a hand-built External Client App, and is billed via Flex Credits that need a sales contact.

best_practice: Language-split llms-full files (platform + JS/Python/Java/Deno) so agents load only the SDK they need.
biggest_gap: No personal token and no DCR: every agent needs a registered Slack app (and often admin approval) before it can touch the API or MCP.

best_practice: Unauthenticated, hosted search-then-retrieve docs MCP over the full OpenAPI surface (two tools, context-efficient) - zero setup before an account exists.
biggest_gap: No OAuth/device login and no hosted product MCP: an agent cannot act on the account without a human pasting the Auth Token; regulatory gates (10DLC/DLT) are unavoidable human work.

best_practice: Ship the CLI with an explicit agent mode (auto JSON on non-TTY, stable error codes, stdin piping, --idempotency-key) and document it on a dedicated 'CLI for AI agents' page.
biggest_gap: No agent-initiated signup or device-flow CLI login; production sending still blocked on domain DNS verification.

best_practice: Granular Restricted API key scopes plus sandbox_mode on the send call for safe agent testing.
biggest_gap: No product MCP, no OAuth/CLI login, and 2FA is mandatory before you can even mint a key.

best_practice: A public magic test token (POSTMARK_API_TEST) documented at the top of llms.txt so agents can validate integrations before any account exists.
biggest_gap: No hosted/OAuth MCP and a human-reviewed account approval before sending to arbitrary recipients.

best_practice: llms.txt line 'Fetch and follow the instructions at build-with-ai.md' leading to an agent-only, validated setup script that tells the agent what NOT to run.
biggest_gap: Productivity MCP must be switched on in the dashboard by a human before OAuth works; signup still a browser form.

best_practice: Published AGENTS-PYTHON.md / AGENTS-JAVASCRIPT.md at the docs root plus a 'Connect to Pinecone' embeddable flow that hands a user's API key to a third-party app.
biggest_gap: Main MCP is local npx with a raw API key; no remote OAuth MCP, so web agents (Claude.ai/ChatGPT) cannot connect without a pasted key.

best_practice: Account creation inside the MCP OAuth screen ('Start without a card') so 'connect the MCP' and 'sign up' are the same step.
biggest_gap: No CLI/device login and hosted DevKit cannot mint tokens, so app code still needs a human to copy a token from the console.

best_practice: Machine-discoverable auth: an unauthenticated 401 points to protected-resource metadata, which leads to an auth.md manifest describing how to sign up and authenticate - no hardcoded endpoints.
biggest_gap: Signup wizard cannot run headless (--ci disabled) and the signup path does not mint a personal API key for REST use.

best_practice: llms.txt starts with imperative instructions for agents ('do not rely on training data, run npx @sentry/agent-plugin install'); the MCP can be scoped to an org/project by URL path
biggest_gap: No anonymous or claimable path. Three token types confuse agents, and docs.sentry.io/ai/mcp returns 404 (MCP docs live on a separate domain)

best_practice: The headless setup CLI falls back cleanly: browser OAuth when interactive, DD_API_KEY/DD_APP_KEY env vars when unattended. MCP toolsets can be selected by query param.
biggest_gap: Region/site fragmentation: every URL depends on the site, and the .md docs render placeholders instead of real endpoints. Personal emails are blocked.

best_practice: Keyless mode: start building with temporary dev keys and claim the account later. Also publishes /.well-known/agent-skills/index.json.
biggest_gap: No product-management MCP (MCP only serves snippets, Beta); workspace/billing/logs only in the dashboard

best_practice: Publishes a measured Agent Experience Score (how well models integrate Auth0 with and without its tools). The MCP init takes `--read-only` and tool-glob scoping.
biggest_gap: No hosted remote MCP, and getting management credentials means creating an M2M app

best_practice: auth.md plus one-shot anonymous environments with a claim ceremony: provision now, attach to a human later
biggest_gap: One-shot creds are test-only; production still needs the claim + dashboard. No one-click MCP deeplinks.

best_practice: Per-client MCP install pages, and splitting the MCP into two domain servers (flags vs AI Configs) to keep tool lists small
biggest_gap: llms.txt links all point to launchdarkly-preview.mintlify.app (looks like a misconfigured or stale preview host); no claimable or anonymous path

best_practice: Separate MCP access models: user-delegated OAuth vs admin-provisioned MCP Configurations with ingress/egress service accounts, so egress creds are never exposed to the agent
biggest_gap: Remote MCP access is off by default for existing orgs; several auth concepts to learn (App Connections, service accounts, MCP configs, DB users)

best_practice: Agent routing guidance in docs ('do not tell the user to create a server first'), plus 'Open in <agent>' deeplinks carrying a full step-by-step setup prompt, plus headless signup with callback-URL paste for agents runnin
biggest_gap: Each downstream app still needs a human OAuth, and MCP calls cost tasks (2 per call) on small free quotas

best_practice: Tiered trust (anonymous -> signed profile -> token) lets agents start with no credential and upgrade; every doc page has a .md twin.
biggest_gap: Completing checkout in-agent requires trusted-tier approval (most agents hand off to continue_url); Universal Cart behind a Google-Form waitlist; shopify.dev lacks a real llms.txt.

best_practice: Doc pages advertise their llms.txt indexes in front-matter (agentTools), and the remote seller MCP lets an existing seller skip developer registration entirely.
biggest_gap: Video-call identity verification for developers; consumer side closed to third-party agents (robots + litigation) while Amazon pushes its own agents.

best_practice: Consumer MCPs scoped to safe read actions (estimates, menus) with booking/payment handed off to the native app.
biggest_gap: No self-serve API for ride requests; no llms.txt/markdown docs; MCP endpoints are per-client paths rather than one open DCR server.

best_practice: Explicit per-agent robots groups (distinguishing user-triggered ChatGPT-User from GPTBot training) is at least a deliberate policy.
biggest_gap: No sanctioned agent surface of any kind; strategic choice to wait for richer agent SDKs.

best_practice: robots.txt explicitly allows the OpenAPI spec while blocking other YAMLs; a dedicated 'Building with AI' guide.
biggest_gap: Feb 2026 dev-mode restrictions (Premium required, 5 users, 1 client ID) and no DCR, so custom agents cannot use the MCP gateway.

best_practice: Same MCP backend serves an auth-free consumer connector and a partner-keyed server; tools/list is declared the source of truth per account.
biggest_gap: Managed Affiliate contract + Account Manager gate; partner terms reportedly restrict AI use without written approval; no order creation tool.

best_practice: Self-access app with client_credentials for a seller's own account avoids redirect-based OAuth.
biggest_gap: No agent surface (MCP/llms.txt) and seller/partner KYC before any credential.

best_practice: llms.txt written as an operating manual for browser agents with explicit confirm-before-order rule; DCR-enabled remote MCP with one-click VS Code install.
biggest_gap: No third-party apps permitted; redirect allowlist breaks DCR for new clients; robots.txt contradicts the llms.txt invitation.

best_practice: A zero-config hosted MCP that sidesteps API-key provisioning entirely by asking the end user to log in through a tool call
biggest_gap: The daily access-token expiry at 6 AM with mandatory 2FA, plus no llms.txt/OpenAPI and no sandbox. Agents trade against real money with no test mode

best_practice: A sandbox with configurable response templates (success/failure/pending) lets an agent test every payment branch deterministically
biggest_gap: No agent surface at all: no MCP, no machine-readable docs, and an unclear path to test credentials without a KYC'd merchant account

best_practice: An llms.txt that tells the agent in its header where llms-full.txt, the markdown variant and the MCP server live, plus an AI-tools page with exact commands for every client
biggest_gap: No product/admin MCP or API for developers to mint sandbox keys; the only product MCP is consumer-facing BillPay

best_practice: Rule-scoped authkeys with an IP whitelist on by default, which limits the blast radius of an agent-held key
biggest_gap: Phone-OTP re-verification just to view or create a key, and a stub llms.txt with no descriptions or markdown pages

best_practice: A user-composed MCP server: pick exactly which apps/tools an agent gets, so least privilege is set at server-creation time
biggest_gap: No CLI/device flow to mint API tokens, and the data-center-specific hosts (zoho.com vs zoho.in) are a common agent failure point

best_practice: The MCP lives on the customer's own subdomain, so tenant routing is implicit with no extra config
biggest_gap: Freshdesk MCP auth is a full-power personal API key in a header, and action quotas are small (100/month on Growth during EAP)

best_practice: Auto-creating a default project + API key the moment a user accepts ToS, plus a 'Coding agent setup' page that ships skills, a docs MCP and machine-readable docs together
biggest_gap: Cloud remote MCP servers require a hand-made OAuth client (no DCR) for Claude/Cursor. Also the key-type migration (unrestricted standard keys rejected) breaks older agent-generated code

best_practice: Keyless Entra ID auth is the recommended default, and the Azure MCP ships as a first-party Claude Code plugin and IDE extensions
biggest_gap: No llms.txt, a heavy signup gate (card + phone), and a 'deploy a model before you can call it' step that agents often miss
